lede: Gold climbed back above $4,100 and Asian stocks rebounded strongly as last week's AI and Middle East jitters faded, while the dollar held most of Friday's payroll-driven gains. Crypto lagged, with ether down more than 4% and bitcoin under $75,000 on worries about tougher rules from a Democrat-led Congress.

focus.text: Up ~1.2% near $4,120 as the dollar pauses after Friday's jobs beat, trading above its 4,068 pivot. Fed speakers today; Tuesday's US CPI is the key risk.
Edging up to 1.1153 after Friday's 0.6% slide on strong US payrolls, still below its 1.1169 pivot. Bailey and Fed speakers today, US CPI on Tuesday.

technicals.indicators: H1 RSI eased to ~48 from ~78 · above daily pivot 4,068.2
technicals.note: The post-midterm rebound from about $3,900 stalled at $4,145 last week; price is back in the upper half of that swing ahead of CPI.

technicals.indicators: MACD below zero but above its signal line · price under the Bollinger mid-band
technicals.note: The broader downtrend from the August high is pausing in a 1.1104–1.1269 band, with Friday's drop pushing price back toward the lower half.
The weekend slide to about $73.7k tested the zone just above the 200-day SMA; price sits mid-way in its 90-day $62.8k–86.6k range.

technicals.indicators: Daily RSI near 40 before the latest leg lower · capped below 2,300 since October
technicals.note: Ether lost its $2,200 shelf over the weekend to hit two-month lows; every rebound since October has failed under $2,300.

calendar.event: China CPI (Oct) – 0.7% y/y vs 0.8% exp; PPI 5.7%

news.text: October's 165k payroll gain, more than double forecasts, lifted CME-implied odds of a December Fed hike to nearly 80%; NY Fed's Williams says inflation remains too high.
Asian equities bounced as AI and Middle East worries cooled: the Nikkei gained over 2.5% and Taiwan recovered after its worst week in two decades; US futures edged up.
Brent eased toward $97.5 after Trump called new strikes on Iran highly unlikely while nuclear talks progress; the benchmark fell more than 13% last week.
Chinese factory-gate prices rose 5.7% y/y in October, the fastest in over four years on energy costs, while consumer inflation cooled to 0.7%.
With eurozone inflation at a three-year high of 4%, Lagarde says the ECB will judge from the data whether to raise rates next month.
Bitcoin and ether sank to their lowest since August late Sunday as traders worried a Democrat-controlled Congress will take a harder line on crypto.
US spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $1.28B over 2–6 Nov and ether funds about $365M; BlackRock's IBIT drove most of Friday's bitcoin outflow.
With BTC below roughly $75,450, Strategy's holdings slip under their average cost; MSCI's final list of index-exclusion candidates, including Strategy, is due Wednesday.
US Treasury's FinCEN moved to cut MEXC off from the US financial system, alleging the exchange handled at least $16B linked to illicit activity.
Ether led weekend losses with a drop of over 4% to about $2,135; XRP and SOL shed 3–4%, extending last week's 6–7% slides.
The withdrawal of the proposed US rule tightening tracking of cross-border crypto transfers takes effect today.

upcoming.note: First remarks since the BoE hike to 4%
Watched for his view on a December hike
US bond market closed; stocks open

week_ahead.intro: Tuesday's October CPI is the week's main test of the near-80% odds of a December Fed hike. AI-linked earnings and the market's read of a Democrat-led Congress add to the risk calendar, while a heavy line-up of central-bank speakers runs through Friday.

themes.text: A hot October print would cement December hike pricing and support the dollar; a soft one could extend gold's rebound.
CoreWeave, Cisco and Applied Materials report after last week's tech rout, testing appetite for AI spending.
Markets weigh Democratic control of Congress: gridlock, debt concerns and a tougher stance on crypto and AI.
Fed speakers daily, ECB's Lane and Lagarde as a December hike is debated, BoE's Bailey, and the CBRT Inflation Report.
US–Iran talks and Hormuz reopening hopes keep Brent under pressure after last week's 13% drop.
